SECTION 6.5. KELLY SIZING
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I use a fractional Kelly on the probability-weighted edge.
  Inputs: p = P(base-or-bull, i.e., the outcome where IV >= price) = 40% + 25%
    = 65%. q = 35% (bear).
  Payoff: if base/bull, expected gain to the probability-weighted IV $411.5
    from $296.55 = +38.8% (b, the win multiple). If bear, loss to $235 =
    -20.7% (a, the loss multiple).
  Full Kelly f* = (p*b - q*a)/(b) ... using the standard form for a binary
    bet: f* = (p*(1+a_win) - 1)/(a_win) is one form; I use the edge/odds form:
    net odds b (win) = 0.388, cost a (loss) = 0.207.
    f* = (p*b - q*a)/b = (0.65*0.388 - 0.35*0.207)/0.388
        = (0.2522 - 0.07245)/0.388 = 0.17975/0.388 = 0.463  -> 46.3% FULL Kelly.
  This is the classic over-concentrated Kelly number. I apply QUARTER Kelly
    (standard for a single, high-uncertainty, single-cycle name with an
    unconfirmed 2027 dollar level and a 35% fat bear):
    Quarter Kelly = 46.3% / 4 = 11.6%.
  RECONCILIATION (Final Rule 13): Layer-5 (capped, crowding-adjusted) = 3.0%.
    Layer-6.5 Quarter-Kelly = 11.6%. Gap = 8.6%p. This is < 20%p, so NO forced
    re-analysis, BUT the two disagree by ~4x in direction of magnitude. The
    binding constraint is the RISK/ARCHETYPE cap (Engine-4 single-cycle,
    crowding, FCF weakness), NOT the Kelly edge. Kelly says "the edge is large
    enough to hold a lot"; the risk framework says "the tail and the
    unconfirmed 2027 level cap you." I take the MINIMUM of the two as the
    defensible size, and split it (see Section 12).
  FINAL SIZE = 3.0% (risk-capped), implemented as a SPLIT entry (Section 12).
